hints: Focus on what Fehling's reagent actually tests for, aldehydes give a brick-red precipitate but ketones do not.
Pick out the two aldehydes from the four structures, then check each one for a chiral carbon with four different groups or a C=C that can show E/Z isomerism.
Look closely at the branched aldehyde for a carbon joined to H, $\text{CH}_3$, $\text{CHO}$ and an alkyl chain, that centre gives optical isomers and completes both conditions.
walkthrough:
**Use Fehling's test to find the functional group**

Great start, Fehling's is your filter here. Only aldehydes are oxidised on warming to give the brick-red $\text{Cu}_2\text{O}$ precipitate.

$$\text{RCHO + 2Cu}^{2+} + 5\text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{RCOO}^- + \text{Cu}_2\text{O(s) + 3H}_2\text{O}$$
Ketones do not react, so we can keep only aldehydes.

**Sort the four structures into aldehydes and ketones**

Look for $-\text{CHO}$ at the end of the chain versus $\text{C=O}$ in the middle. A and D end in $-\text{CHO}$, so they are aldehydes. B and C have $\text{C=O}$ in the middle, so they are ketones and cannot give the precipitate.

**Test the aldehydes for stereoisomerism**

Now check A for E/Z and chirality. A is $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C=CHCH}_2\text{CHO}$. The left C of the $\text{C=C}$ has two identical $\text{CH}_3$ groups, so no E/Z isomerism, and there is no carbon with four different groups, so no optical isomerism.

D is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH(CH}_3)\text{CHO}$, or 2-methylpentanal. Carbon 2 is joined to $\text{H}$, $\text{CH}_3$, $\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ and $\text{CHO}$, four different groups, so it is chiral and shows optical isomerism.

**Conclude the structure**

Only D satisfies both clues at once. It is an aldehyde, so positive to Fehling's, and it has a chiral centre, so it has stereoisomers (a pair of enantiomers).

options.A: A is 4-methylpent-3-enal, an aldehyde so it would give the Fehling's precipitate. However it has no stereoisomers because the $\text{C=C}$ has two identical methyl groups on one carbon, preventing E/Z isomerism, and it has no chiral centre.
options.B: B is hex-4-en-2-one, a ketone so it gives no reaction with Fehling's reagent. Although its $\text{C=C}$ ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH=CH-}$) could show E/Z isomerism, it fails the essential functional group test.
options.C: C is 3-methylpentan-2-one, a ketone so it gives no reaction with Fehling's reagent. It does have a chiral centre at C3 and therefore has optical isomers, but failing Fehling's rules it out.
options.D: D is 2-methylpentanal, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH(CH}_3)\text{CHO}$. The terminal $-\text{CHO}$ group makes it an aldehyde, so it is oxidised by Fehling's on warming to give red $\text{Cu}_2\text{O}$. C2 is chiral with H, $\text{CH}_3$, $\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ and $\text{CHO}$ attached, so it exists as a pair of optical isomers. It meets both conditions.
